problems.title: Combine fractional powers
problems.question: Evaluate cube-root(2√5)·sixth-root(16/5).
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The powers of5 cancel and the powers of2 add to1. The product is2.

problems.title: Order powers of a small negative number
problems.question: Order a,a²,a³,a⁴ increasingly if a=2−√5.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: Odd powers are negative and even powers positive. Because |a|<1,the magnitude decreases as the exponent increases.
Thus a<a³<a⁴<a².

problems.title: Lines determined by point pairs
problems.question: How many lines pass through pairs of40 points,no three collinear?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: Every pair gives one line,and no line is counted by another pair because no three points are collinear. The count is780.

problems.title: Digits in a least common multiple
problems.question: How many digits has the least positive integer divisible by1 through12?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: LCM uses the highest required prime powers: $2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7$.
steps: The product is2520,a four-digit integer.

problems.title: Count divisors from prime exponents
problems.question: How many positive divisors has A=250³·54²?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: Thus A=2⁵·3⁶·5⁹. A divisor independently chooses the three exponents in6,7,10 ways.
The count is6·7·10=420.

problems.title: Primes in a short interval
problems.question: How many primes lie from111 to130?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: For n≤130,it is enough to test prime divisors2,3,5,7,11.
steps: The primes in the interval are113 and127.
The other odd candidates are111,117,123,129 (multiples of3),115,125 (multiples of5),119=7·17,and121=11². Even candidates are composite.

problems.title: Compare reciprocals by taking a ratio
problems.question: x is25% greater than y. How many times as large is1/y as1/x?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The reciprocal ratio is1.25.
problems.note: The comparison presumes nonzero positive quantities,as usual in a percentage word problem.

problems.title: Common divisors are divisors of the gcd
problems.question: A is the set of divisors of45 and B of126. Sum the elements of A∩B.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The common positive divisors are1,3,9. Their sum is13.

problems.title: Preserve dry matter when drying apples
problems.question: Fresh apples are72% water,dried apples1/15 water. How many kg of dried apples result from40 kg fresh?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The dry material weighs11.2 kg. It forms14/15 of the dried mass.

problems.title: Compare a composition’s constant terms
problems.question: f(x)=2x+1,g(x)=x²−t,and f(g(x))=2x²−3. Find t.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The constant term satisfies−2t+1=−3,so t=2.

problems.title: Count prime factors in a factorial
problems.question: Factor all integers1 through199. How many factors7 appear in total?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: There are28 multiples of7,including4 multiples of49 that each supply one additional7. No multiple of343 occurs.

problems.title: Bus count is inverse to time spacing
problems.question: There are12 equally spaced buses on a circular route. How many must be added to reduce the time gap by1/5?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: For a fixed circuit time T,the gap is T/N. New gap=(4/5)(T/12).
steps: The new count satisfies N=12·5/4=15. Thus add15−12=3 buses.

problems.title: Last digit using short power cycles
problems.question: Find the last digit of199¹²−12¹⁹⁹.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: Since199≡3 modulo4,2¹⁹⁹ has last digit8.
The difference ends in1−8≡3 modulo10.

problems.title: Bounds for a linear combination
problems.question: Given2<a<5 and−3<b<−1,find the range of A=3a−2b.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: Adding gives8<A<21. Every interior value is attainable because the expression is continuous on the parameter rectangle.

problems.title: A zero numerator still needs a valid denominator
problems.question: How many roots has (x³−4x²+4x)/√(x−2)=0?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The only numerator zeros are0 and2. Neither lies in x>2,so the original equation has no real roots.

problems.title: Two supplementary neighbours of one angle
problems.question: An angle’s two adjacent supplementary angles sum to120°. Find the angle.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: If the angle isθ,each neighbour is180°−θ.

problems.title: Triangle of median midpoints
problems.question: A triangle has perimeter12. Find the perimeter of the triangle joining its three median midpoints.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: For vertex vectors A,B,C,the midpoint on the A-median is $(2A+B+C)/4$.
steps: Subtract two such midpoint vectors: their difference is one quarter of the corresponding original side vector.
All new sides have one quarter of the original lengths,so the perimeter is12/4=3 cm.

problems.title: Intersecting chords and opposite arcs
problems.question: Chords AB,CD meet inside a circle at M,angle AMC=40°. Arc AD is20° larger than arc BC. Find arc AD.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The two arcs sum to280°. Let arcBC=t,arcAD=t+20°.
Then2t+20=280,giving t=130° and arcAD=150°.

problems.title: Two tangent circles inside a sixty-degree angle
problems.question: Two externally tangent circles lie inside a60° angle and touch both sides. The smaller radius is4. Find the larger radius.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: Circle centres lie on the angle bisector at distances r/sin30°=2r from the vertex.
steps: The centre separation is2R−2r and also R+r by external tangency. Thus2R−2r=R+r,giving R=3r=12.

problems.title: An exponential antiderivative with a negative logarithm
problems.question: Which listed expression can equal ∫(0.5)^x dx?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: An antiderivative is C−1/(2^x ln2)=C−(log₂e)/2^x.
The listed expression with C=1 is1−(log₂e)/2^x.

problems.title: Number of sides from equal interior angles
problems.question: Every interior angle of a polygon is170°. How many sides?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: The exterior turning angle is180°−170°=10°; exterior angles sum to360°.

problems.title: Circumradius of a shallow isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base12 and altitude4. Find circumradius.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: Its area is12·4/2=24. Therefore R=12·52/(4·24)=6.5 cm.

problems.title: Trapezoid diagonals have equal division ratios
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD,diagonals meet at O,OC=6 and OD:OB=3:2. Find AO.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: Similarity of triangles AOD and COB gives $AO/OC=OD/OB$.
steps: Therefore AO/6=3/2,and AO=9.

problems.title: Lengths of parallel trisection segments
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD with bases BC=5,AD=11,the legs are trisected in matching order to give MK,NL. Find MK+NL.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: Parallel-section length varies linearly between the base lengths.
steps: The matching segments are at one third and two thirds of the height from BC.
Their lengths are5+(11−5)/3=7 and5+2(11−5)/3=9. Sum=16.

problems.title: Check consistency before using periodicity
problems.question: f has period2 and f(x)=|x| on the closed interval[−2.5,−0.5]. Find f(2π+3).
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: Periodicity requires $f(-2.5)=f(-0.5)$,since the inputs differ by2.
steps: The stated formula instead gives2.5 and0.5. Therefore no function satisfies every printed condition.
If the interval was intended to be half-open,reduce2π+3 by10 to2π−7∈(−2.5,−0.5). Its absolute value is7−2π.
problems.answer: As printed,no such function. Intended half-open-interval answer:7−2π.
problems.note: The closed endpoints conflict with the stated period. The explanation retains this issue rather than silently changing the question.

problems.title: Create an odd function from any function
problems.question: Which expression is odd for every real-domain function f?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: Substituting−x reverses the two terms. Thus the difference is always odd. The sum f(x)+f(−x) is always even instead.

problems.title: A rational integral by a linear substitution
problems.question: Evaluate the definite integral of 2(x+1)/(2x−1)³ from1 to2.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The limits become1 and3. The integral is(1/2)∫₁³(u⁻²+3u⁻³)du.
An antiderivative is−1/(2u)−3/(4u²). At3 it is−1/4;at1 it is−5/4. Difference=1.

problems.title: Intersect two linear inequality solutions
problems.question: Solve7(x+1)−2x>9−4x and3(5−2x)−1≥4−5x.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: The first simplifies to9x>2;the second to10≥x.
steps: Thus x>2/9 and x≤10. Their intersection is(2/9,10].

problems.title: Use the ratio between the two radicals
problems.question: Evaluate (x/y−y/x)·[1−(x−2y)/(x−y)]÷(1+x/y),for y=√52,x=√13.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The middle ratio is(x−4x)/(x−2x)=3,so its bracket is−2.
The whole value is(−3/2)·(−2)/(3/2)=2. All denominators are nonzero.

problems.title: Maximise two fractions simultaneously
problems.question: Maximise14/(9x²−12xy+4y²+7)+12/(|5x−3y−1|+3).
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The two terms are at most2 and4,so their sum is at most6.
Equality requires3x−2y=0 and5x−3y−1=0. Solving gives x=2,y=3,so the upper bound is attained.

problems.title: Midline of a trapezoid with perpendicular diagonals
problems.question: A trapezoid has perpendicular diagonals;one is8 and the other makes30° with a base. Find midline.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: The length-8 diagonal makes60° with the base. Thus height h=8sin60°=4√3.
steps: The other diagonal has length h/sin30°=8√3. The sum of their horizontal projections equals the sum of the bases.
That sum is8cos60°+8√3cos30°=4+12=16. The midline is half of it,8.

problems.title: Area under an exponential
problems.question: Find area bounded by y=e^x,x=0,x=ln7,y=0.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: The area is7−1=6.

problems.title: Clock hands repeat an acute separation
problems.question: The acute angle between clock hands isα now and wasα eight minutes ago. Findα.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: Equal smaller angles occur on opposite sides of an alignment,so the relative change is2α or360°−2α.
The acute condition excludes the second possibility,which would giveα=158°. Hence2α=44°,soα=22°.

problems.title: Find prime parameters using integer divisibility
problems.question: Find primes q for which6x²−12x+3=q(x−2) has an integer root.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
steps: An integer q requires t to divide3,so t∈{1,−1,3,−3}.
These give q=21,3,31,−7 respectively. The prime values are3 and31,attained at x=1 and5.

problems.title: Meeting times before and after speed changes
problems.question: Two cyclists meet36min after leaving opposite towns. The first then doubles speed,the second reduces speed10%. The first arrives6min later. Find first total travel time.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into a simple calculation and check any restrictions.
formulas: Let r=v₂/v₁>0. Remaining distances after meeting are36v₂ and36v₁.
steps: The first’s remaining time is18r;the second’s is36/(0.9r)=40/r minutes.
Thus18r=40/r+6,or9r²−3r−20=0. Its positive root is5/3.
The first needs18·5/3=30 further minutes,so total time is36+30=66min.
